title: The 1919 streetcar strike parade and the broken cornet
summary: Lala tells how he played behind strike speakers with Schilling in 1919, walked back, smashed his cornet on a post and had to borrow Joe Hall's for work.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: They had circles that week. I'm going to tell you, the last parade I've prayed in my life. The last time I prayed. It was in 1919, they had a car strike. See? And we had to walk from the heritage, we were all human, you see? But we had to hide outside men. So, Shilling got a job. Around 1919. 18 or 19. Because they would have a meet at the old Crescent Theatre. You know the Crescent Theatre? You don't remember the Crescent Theatre? Tulane and Tulane. Tulane, Tulane, yeah. All right. So, Shilling says, come on. I said, I ain't playing no other things. I'm going to talk. Come on, man. We got to. All right. So, we walked from the Arabella barn, you know where that's at? To the Tulane Theatre. Okay. Well, when we got there, after every talker, we had to play a little, little talker, little run music behind them. So, after they won the strike, well, they decided to give us what they all kind of wanted to march back. You know? Oh, I said, no, I can't walk back. Oh, yeah, come on, man. I didn't want to be disagreeable. I said, I had to go to work that night. You said, I was working at the window right now. I forgot the window. Well, I walked back by the horse. When I got to the car bar and I took my trumpet and I wrapped it on the post. I mean, I broke it. I bent it. I broke it. I broke it. I got so mad. Guess what? I had to get a carnet that night to go to work. I had to go borrow Joe Hall's carnet. He had just bought a new carnet and he didn't use it, you know? I had to go borrow his carnet to go to work that night. I couldn't get a carnet no way. And that's the last parade I walked in.
